purpose: Verify from public text TOAs, without dynamic-spectrum pickle execution, that the approximately 44-minute cadence is independently visible in separate telescope epochs before any deeper morphology interpretation.

simple_cadence_replay.method: Within each dense same-instrument observing sequence, compute consecutive MJD differences and convert days to seconds. This is a deliberately simple cadence sanity check, not a replacement for PINT, barycentric corrections, dispersion treatment or pulse-phase modeling.

TOPA_interpretation: The long-period cadence is directly recoverable from public TOA sequences at two independent radio facilities without relying on a visual pattern claim.

The simple interval averages differ slightly from the fitted ephemeris because TOAs are not an ideal clock and the public timing model includes barycentric/dispersion/timing treatment absent from this sanity replay.
Agreement at the sub-0.1-percent level is sufficient for the present gate: the approximately 44-minute recurrence is real and instrument-independent.
This promotes periodicity/existence only. It does not identify the compact object, emission mechanism, intelligence, or message content.
